stats.title: # Verification coverage
stats.legend: "Verified" = tried on the real app; "Partial" = only one side checked; "Cannot verify" = reason recorded; "Assumption" = not tried. TC = written test cases. "PO decided" = answered by the Product Owner.

srs.audience: This document is for the Product Owner, the development team, testers (QA), legal and other stakeholders. Every requirement has a code (UC, BR, AC, TC) so it can be quoted directly in tickets and test scripts.
srs.scope_modules: The document covers %d business modules with %d use cases: %s.
gloss_rows: A system function described by actors, main event flow and alternate flows; code UC-<module>.<feature>
Acceptance criterion in Given/When/Then form, code AC-<module>.<feature>.<number>
srs.overview_intro: This document follows the IEEE 830 structure and has four parts:
parts: Part 1: Introduction: purpose, scope, glossary and reading conventions.
Part 2: Functional requirements: actors, function list, use case diagrams, business processes and detailed specification of each use case.
Part 3: Non-functional requirements: user interface, security and compliance, constraints.
Part 4: Appendices: bugs found during verification, open issues, integration and data model of each module.
srs.uc_explain: Each use case in section 2.6 has: a function specification table (code, actor, description, trigger, preconditions, main and alternate event flows, postconditions), an input data table, and supplementary specification (business rules, formulas, state lifecycle, permissions, UI states, edge cases, module links, audit log, acceptance criteria, test cases, open questions). In the data table the template's "Example" column is replaced by an "Error message" column; example values are in the test cases.
